articles.title: Two Carlton players treated in hospital after off-season night out
articles.summary: Club issues brief statement about Lachie Cowan and Will Hayward, saying latter suffered minor cut to head after a fall. An off-season night out for Carlton football club teammates ended with two players admitted to hospital for treatment on Sunday morning, in what the club says are “separate…
body: The club released a statement on Sunday confirming that AFL players Lachie Cowan, 21, and Will Hayward, 27, had been treated and discharged, after reports in several media outlets about the aftermath of an off-season night out. Guardian Australia understands both players were both part of a larger group that had been socialising on Saturday evening.
The club statement said Cowan had “received medical treatment and underwent observation, before being discharged a short time later” but did not provide any more information about the circumstances.
Hayward was also admitted to hospital later on Sunday morning, after returning home.
“Will Hayward experienced a minor cut to the head after a fall, and admitted himself to hospital where he received stitches before being discharged,” Carlton said.

articles.title: Bezzecchi wins as Martin retakes championship lead
articles.summary: Marco Bezzecchi triumphs at the Indonesian Grand Prix, while Jorge Martin finishes third to retake the lead from Marc Marquez in the MotoGP world championship.
body: Italian Bezzecchi made his move on pole-sitter Raul Fernandez with nine laps to go at a sweltering Mandalika International Circuit.
Fernandez finished second ahead of compatriot Martin, with the Spanish duo locking out the podium for Italian manufacturer Aprilia.
Ducati's reigning seven-time world champion Marquez finished sixth, losing the championship lead he had taken for the first time this season by winning Saturday's sprint race.
Fernandez and Bezzecchi had clashed and crashed out in that race, with the Spaniard needing to brake with his middle finger for the whole of Sunday's race after fracturing his index finger.

articles.title: Williams strikes out 12 as Guardians blank White Sox to complete ALDS comeback
articles.summary: Williams fans 12 as Cleveland win decisive Game 5. Ramírez’s two-run homer provides only scoring. Guardians to face Rays for place in World Series. Gavin Williams struck out 12, José Ramírez homered on a pitch just above home plate and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Chicago White Sox 2-0 on…
body: Cleveland open the American League Championship Series at Tampa Bay on Monday night, seeking their first World Series appearance since 2016. The Guardians/Indians franchise have not won the title since 1948, the longest drought among MLB teams.
Guardians pitchers struck out 21, the most in a nine-inning postseason game. The White Sox managed just three hits, putting only nine balls in play, and struck out 75 times over the series.

Two days after getting the save in Game 4, Williams became just the third pitcher in postseason history to get the last out of a game and start the following game when his team faced elimination in both.

He did not allow a hit until Kyle Teel looped a knuckle-curve into right field with two outs in the sixth, two innings after Ramírez homered for the second straight game, a two-run drive off Sean Burke.

articles.title: Kipchoge, 41, breaks course record at Melbourne Marathon
articles.summary: Double Olympic champion Eliud Kipchoge says "his body is still peaking" after winning the Melbourne Marathon in a course record time at the age of 41.
body: The Kenyan crossed the line in two hours nine minutes 10 seconds for his 17th career win over the distance and first since the Berlin Marathon in 2023.
"I believe that my body is still peaking - still able to compete with the next generation," Kipchoge said.
"The oldest athlete is still competing but I am happy to run with the Gen Zs."
The course was partly raced along the Australian Formula One track at Albert Park and finished inside the iconic Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG).

articles.title: Ulster need 'honest conversations' after winless start
articles.summary: Ulster hooker Tom Stewart admits "I don't think I've come to the party well enough" and says the squad must have "honest conversations" after an underwhelming start to the season.
body: Successive draws with Glasgow and Munster after a loss to Edinburgh leaves Ulster winless in the United Rugby Championship before starting their Challenge Cup campaign away to Zebre next week.

Head coach Richie Murphy said he was "bitterly disappointed" after his side were forced to fight back for a 26-26 draw with Munster, while Stewart questioned his own contributions to the game in Belfast.

"From a personal point of view, I'm not happy with my performances about it. I don't think I've come to the party well enough, I don't know if it's my preparation or the mental side to the game," said Stewart, who captained Ulster against Glasgow and Munster in the injured Iain Henderson's absence.
"It's something I really need to have a look at and plan better or whatever it is, but I need to start understanding why that is the case."

articles.title: UN Human Rights Office calls racist abuse directed at Coco Gauff ‘appalling’
articles.summary: The United Nations has condemned people who sent racist abuse to Coco Gauff after she followed the rules of tennis correctly at the China Open in Beijing. The 22-year-old American was sent what she called an “insane” amount of comments and direct messages after stopping a point mid-rally against…
body: On Saturday, the UN’s Human Rights office issued a statement calling the abuse “appalling” and asking sports leagues to stand up for targeted players.

“Racist messages such as those targeting tennis player Coco Gauff online are appalling and illustrate that Black female athletes are specifically targeted for vitriol and racial abuse,” the organization wrote in a statement posted on X.

“There is no place in sport for racial or sexist slurs and abuse. Players, coaches, and sports bodies need to stand up for those facing such attacks and fans need to push back against those who sully sport with racism and sexism.”
Gauff, a two-time Grand Slam champion, had stopped a point to video review a possible hindrance as Sun prepared to hit a winner.

articles.title: ‘Why are you ashamed?’ – A’ja Wilson’s act of growing up under privileged hammered by Craig Carton
articles.summary: Craig Carton has criticised A’ja Wilson over comments about her childhood after the Las Vegas Aces star collected her fifth WNBA MVP award. Wilson reflected on her journey during her MVP acceptance speech and said that at 15 she was more focused on surviving than dreaming about becoming a five-time…
body: The comments drew attention because Wilson attended Heathwood Hall Episcopal School in South Carolina, and Carton argued that her upbringing did not match the hardship suggested by her remarks.
Carton addressed the controversy on The Craig Carton Show and took particular issue with Wilson describing herself as simply trying to survive.

“She was trying to survive at 15 years old? How to survive the mean streets of Columbia, South Carolina? Interesting! But I know something you. You went to Heathwood Hall; that’s a private school,” Carton said.

He added, “Why is A’ja Wilson trying to cosplay that she grew up on the streets of South Carolina or poor or disenfranchised or without a mom and a dad to raise her without love when the exact opposite is actually true.

articles.title: Brennan holds on for one-shot victory at Baycurrent Classic in Japan
articles.summary: Michael Brennan won the Baycurrent Classic for his second victory of the season and third on the PGA Tour, parring the final six holes for a three-under 68 and a one-stroke margin over Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell.
body: Tied for the third-round lead with Bridgeman and Zach Bauchou in the FedEx Cup Fall event, Brennan rebounded from a bogey on the 10th with birdies on holes 11 and 12 before the winning par run at hilly Yokohama Country Club.
His best par save came on the par-3 16th when he hit a long shot from a greenside bunker to a foot. He finished at 16-under 268.

Bridgeman missed a chance to pull even on the par-4 17th when his five-foot birdie putt slid by to the right. On the par-4 18th, he had a 55-foot birdie putt over a large ridge that he left four feet wide. He shot a 69.
Mitchell was two strokes ahead after playing a five-hole stretch in five under with three birdies and an eagle. He then played the final 10 in two over for a 68.

articles.title: Eliud Kipchoge wins first marathon in three years with record-breaking Melbourne run
articles.summary: Eliud Kipchoge rolled back the years as he won his first marathon in three years, setting a new course record in Melbourne in the process. The 41-year-old, making his debut in Melbourne, eclipsed the previous course benchmark by two seconds as he completed the race in 2:09:10, and was mobbed by…
body: The Kenyan spent more than an hour celebrating with fans and signing autographs at the scene of his first marathon victory since Berlin in September 2023.
His compatriot Timothy Kiplagat Ronoh had set the previous record in 2022.

Kipchoge, a two-time Olympic champion and former world record holder, broke away from Jimmy Whelan with just over 10km to go and powered to the line solo, slowing down to wave to fans inside the cricket ground before the finish.
He said: “The crowd is so wonderful – I’ve never seen a crowd like this. Melbourne is really, really a sporting city.

articles.title: Carrick must share burden of Man Utd's failings with his players
articles.summary: "We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it." A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.
body: Stuck in the mire of Manchester United's worst start to a league season for 40 years, the manager appeared lost for legitimate reasons. His margin for error is shrinking by the week.
Why were his side outplayed at home by the Premier League's bottom club? Why can't they hold onto leads? Why do they seem incapable of playing against 10 men?

All of these are fair questions to put to the man himself and many were asked of Carrick in the wake of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Spurs. None were answered with enough detail to satisfy, though, only really serving to hold a mirror up to what was delivered on the pitch: inadequacy.

Clearly the manager can only accept so much of the blame. His players are yet to offer a single complete performance, only bit-part displays of individualism and self-direction. Where is the cohesiveness that shaped the backend of last year? What happened to the clarity that transformed a broken season into a third-place finish?
points: "We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game.
With the ball, without the ball, we were off it.
A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.

articles.title: Van Gerwen dumped out of Swiss Darts Trophy as nightmare year goes on
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen's nightmare year went from bad to worse as he was dumped out of the Swiss Darts Trophy in his opening match by Mensur Suljovic 6-4 on Saturday night.
body: Suljovic led 5-2 before Van Gerwen threatened a comeback but three missed darts to force a decider allowed Suljovic to take advantage.
It was Suljovic's fourth straight win over Van Gerwen and the fifth time in six tournaments that the Dutchman has exited after one match.
Luke Humphries, Gian van Veen and Jonny Clayton all advanced to Finals Day as ten seeds crashed out on a remarkable day of action in Basel.
Newly crowned World Grand Prix champion Humphries was among the headline acts on Day Two at the St. Jakobshalle, where he prevailed against Kevin Doets.
